interactions.summary: Jiang asks the class to imagine the worst violation against God and nature, introduces incest as the missing comparison case, and then links incest and homosexuality through elite exclusion and the blocking of social mobility.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang says incest is implicit rather than explicit in the canto, so part of the reading task is imaginative completion.

claims.claim: Jiang proposes incest as the truly paradigmatic violence against God and nature and says its absence from the explicit text forces readers to imagine it as part of the same zone.
A student links incest and homosexuality by saying both involve sex with one's own kind, and Jiang turns that into a social logic of exclusion.
Jiang says the real social function of elite homosexuality and incest is to preserve privilege by excluding others and blocking openness and social mobility.

signature_moments.moment: Sexual sameness is recoded as a politics of exclusion.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the purpose of this is to exclude other people
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the decisive turn from private desire to social structure in Jiang's interpretation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The social openness Jiang says elite self-enclosure prevents, making the sin civilizational rather than merely private.

chronology_notes.note: This packet is the main breakthrough in the lecture's argument: the issue becomes exclusionary elite self-reproduction rather than sex alone.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's ranking of incest and bestiality is rhetorical and exploratory; preserve the comparison as part of his classroom reasoning rather than as a stable doctrine.
